source_text: Gloriosissimis imperatoribus Honorio duodecimo et Theodosio octauo consulibus duodecimo Kalendas Octobres Caesareae in ecclesia maiore cum Deuterius episcopus metropolitanus Caesariensis una cum Alypio Tagastensi, Augustino Hipponiensi, Possidio Calamensi, Rustico Cartenitano, Palladio Tigabitano et ceteris episcopis in exedram processissent praesentibus presbyteris et diaconibus et uniuerso clero ac frequentissima plebe, adesset etiam Emeritus partis Donati episcopus, Augustinus episcopus ecclesiae catholicae dixit: Fratres carissimi, qui ab initio catholici fuistis et quicumque ad catholicam ex Donatistarum errore uenistis et pacem huius sanctae ecclesiae catholicae cognouistis et ueraci corde tenuistis et qui adhuc forte de catholicae unitatis ueritate dubitatis, audite nos sollicitos pura dilectione pro uobis. quando uenit ad hanc ciuitatem die nudiustertiana frater noster Emeritus Donatistarum adhuc episcopus, perlatum est ad nos subito eum esse praesentem. et quoniam caritate quam deus uidet desiderabamus eius praesentiam, ad eum uidendum continuo conuolauimus. inuenimus eum stantem in platea; facta inuicem salutatione admonuimus, quod durum esset ac turpe eum in platea remanere, ut ad ecclesiam nobiscum ueniret. at ille nobis sine ulla recusatione consensit; ubi nos putauimus eum ita communionem catholicam non recusaturum, quemadmodum uel spontaneum obtulit aduentum uel ad ecclesiam uenire minime dubitauit. illo autem in peruersitate haeretica quamuis intra ecclesiam catholicam diutius remorante allocutus sum dilectionem uestram, sicut meminisse dignamini. multa dixi, quae audistis et quae sine dubio quantum potestis etiam meministis, multa de pace, multa de caritate, multa de sanctae ecclesiae catholicae quam deus promisit et praestitit unitate. in quo meo sermone et uos alloquebar et illum exhortabar et, quantum in me poterant uiscera caritatis, omnes in periculo animae suae constitutos in illo meo sermone parturiebam et parere domino cupiebam. hoc enim et beatus Paulus apostolus dixit quibusdam: filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec Christus formetur in uobis. sed etiam post sermonem nostrum cum adhuc in illa sua perduraret pertinacia, nec sic desperandum putauimus; sed nec de quoquam, quamdiu uiuit in hoc corpore, homine desperandum putamus. neque enim sic dixi nudiustertius me non desperasse, ut hodie audeam desperare.
thought_title: Augustine recounts Emeritus's arrival and his own pastoral address
orientation: Augustine, Catholic bishop of Hippo, is speaking to the assembled church at Caesarea, with Emeritus the Donatist bishop present, and he is recounting what happened when Emeritus came to the city two days earlier.
pass_a_gloss: To the most glorious emperors Honorius for the twelfth time and Theodosius for the eighth time consuls, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October, at Caesarea in the greater church, when Deuterius metropolitan bishop of Caesarea together with Alypius of Tagaste, Augustine of Hippo, Possidius of Calama, Rusticus of Cartenna, Palladius of Tigava and the rest of the bishops had proceeded into the exedra, in the presence of the presbyters and deacons and the whole clergy and a very crowded people, and Emeritus, bishop of the party of Donatus, was also present, Augustine bishop of the catholic church said: Dearest brothers, [you] who from the beginning were catholics, and all [you] who have come to the catholic [church] from the error of the Donatists and have known the peace of this holy catholic church and have held [it] with a true heart, and [you] who still perhaps doubt about the truth of catholic unity, hear us [who are] anxious with pure love for you. When our brother Emeritus, still bishop of the Donatists, came to this city on the day before yesterday, it was reported to us suddenly that he was present. And since with the love which God sees we were desiring his presence, we flew together immediately to see him. We found him standing in the street; after a mutual greeting was made, we admonished [him] that it was hard and shameful for him to remain in the street, that he should come with us to the church. And he consented to us without any refusal; where we thought that he would not refuse catholic communion in the same way as he offered [his] arrival either of his own accord or did not hesitate at all to come to the church. But while he was lingering in heretical perversity, although within the catholic church, for a rather long time, I addressed your love, as you deign to remember. I said many things, which you heard and which without doubt as much as you can you also remember, many things about peace, many things about love, many things about the unity of the holy catholic church which God promised and bestowed. In that my sermon I was both addressing you and exhorting him and, as far as the bowels of love could [do] in me, I was in labor with all [those] placed in danger of their soul in that my sermon and was desiring to bring [them] forth to the Lord. For this also the blessed Paul the apostle said to certain [people]: my little children, whom I am again in labor with, until Christ is formed in you. But even after our sermon, when he was still persisting in that his obstinacy, not even so did we think [it] to be despaired of; but neither about any man, as long as he lives in this body, do we think [it] to be despaired of. For I did not say the day before yesterday that I had not despaired in such a way that today I would dare to despair.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'Catholic fold' for gremium catholicum, not 'Catholic communion'.
The glossary requires 'Donatist party' for pars Donati.

Here communio refers to fellowship in the Catholic Church, and the glossary's banned list applies to gremium catholicum, not to communio; 'Catholic communion' is the natural rendering for communio catholica.
The Latin uiscera is a strong physical metaphor for deep affection; 'bowels' preserves the literal force.
The verb parturio means to be in labor or travail; the metaphor of childbirth is central to the Pauline allusion.
Nudiustertianus means 'of the day before yesterday'; the English phrase is the standard equivalent.

bible_refs.note: filoli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec Christus formetur in uobis

pass_b_english: In the consulship of the most glorious emperors Honorius for the twelfth time and Theodosius for the eighth, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October, at Caesarea in the greater church, Deuterius, metropolitan bishop of Caesarea, together with Alypius of Thagaste, Augustine of Hippo, Possidius of Calama, Rusticus of Cartenna, Palladius of Tigabitanus, and the other bishops, came forward into the hall, with the presbyters, deacons, the whole clergy, and a very large crowd of people present. Emeritus, bishop of the Donatist party, was also there. Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said:

Dearest brothers, you who have been Catholics from the beginning, and all of you who have come to the Catholic Church from the error of the Donatists and have come to know the peace of this holy Catholic Church and have held it with a true heart, and you who perhaps still doubt the truth of Catholic unity: listen to us, who are anxious for you with pure love. When our brother Emeritus, still a bishop of the Donatists, came to this city the day before yesterday, it was suddenly reported to us that he was present. And since we longed for his presence with the love that God sees, we hurried at once to see him. We found him standing in the street. After we greeted one another, we urged him that it would be harsh and shameful for him to remain in the street, and that he should come with us to the church. He agreed without any refusal. There we thought he would not refuse the Catholic fold, just as he had either offered his coming of his own accord or had not hesitated at all to come to the church. But while he lingered in heretical perversity, even though inside the Catholic Church, I spoke to your love, as you are good enough to remember. I said many things, which you heard and which without doubt you also remember as much as you can: many things about peace, many about love, many about the unity of the holy Catholic Church, which God promised and has brought about. In that sermon of mine I was speaking to you and exhorting him, and as far as the bowels of love could work in me, I was in labor with all who were placed in danger of their souls, and I longed to give birth to them for the Lord. For the blessed apostle Paul also said to certain people: 'My little children, with whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you' (Galatians 4:19). But even after our sermon, when he still persisted in his stubbornness, we did not think we should despair even then. Nor do we think we should despair of any person, as long as he lives in this body. For I did not say the day before yesterday that I had not despaired, only to dare to despair today.

problems.why: lint glossary: banned rendering of gremium catholicum; use 'Catholic fold' ('Catholic communion')

edits.old: he would not refuse Catholic communion
edits.new: he would not refuse the Catholic fold

fixed: The English 'Catholic communion' renders 'communionem catholicam' (source: 'communionem catholicam non recusaturum'), not 'gremium catholicum'. The glossary entry for 'gremium catholicum' bans 'Catholic communion' as a rendering of that specific phrase, but here the source word is 'communio', whose glossary entry gives 'communion' as the English. The English is correct and should not be changed.

last_rejected.why: Tigabitano is ablative of Tigabitanus; 'of Tigabitanus' treats the see name as a personal name rather than using adjectival form.
last_rejected.fix: Palladius of Tigabitana, or Palladius the Tigabitan
last_rejected.ruling: 'Of Tigabitanus' correctly renders the ablative see-name; standard episcopal formula, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: we did not think we should despair even then
last_rejected.why: Latin says 'we did not think despair was called for even in this situation,' not 'we did not think we should despair.'
last_rejected.fix: we did not think that even so there was cause for despair
last_rejected.ruling: 'We did not think we should despair' accurately renders 'nec sic desperandum putauimus'; no meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: For I did not say the day before yesterday that I had not despaired, only to dare to despair today
last_rejected.source_quote: neque enim sic dixi nudiustertius me non desperasse, ut hodie audeam desperare
last_rejected.why: Misreads syntax: 'I did not say [on the day before yesterday that I had not despaired] in order that today I might dare to despair' should be 'I did not speak thus on the day before yesterday, that I had not despaired, so that today I should dare to despair.'
last_rejected.fix: For I did not say on the day before yesterday that I had not despaired, so that today I might dare to despair
last_rejected.ruling: English conveys same meaning: 'I did not say...that I had not despaired, only to dare to despair today'; no real error.
